docs.text: dot-annotated-services Dotkernel component used to create services through any PSR-11 container, such as Laminas Service Manager , and inject them with dependencies just using method annotations. Annotation parsing can be cached to improve performance. This package can clean up your code by getting rid of all the factories you write, sometimes just to inject a dependency or two. Documentation Documentation is available at: https://docs.dotkernel.org/dot-annotated-services/. Version History Branch PSR-11 Docblock Comments OSS Lifecycle PHP Version 6.0 1 || 2 Annotations 5.0 1 || 2 Attributes 4.0 1 Annotations 3.0 1 Annotations Versions 4.x and 6.0 are the proper releases of this package. They are annotation-based. Version 5.x is discontinued. It used PHP attributes, which are now provided by a separate package: dot-dependency-injection ( documentation ). Use it if you want attributes instead of annotations. See Version 5 is discontinued for migration notes. Badges Installation Run the following command in your project directory composer require dotkernel/dot-annotated-services Usage Using the AnnotatedServiceFactory You can register services in the container using the AnnotatedServiceFactory as below. return [ 'factories' => [ ServiceClass::class => AnnotatedServiceFactory::class, ], ]; You can use only the fully qualified class name as the service key. The next step is to annotate the service constructor or setters with the service names to inject. use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject; /** * @Inject({ * Dependency1::class, * Dependency2::class, * "config" * }) */ public function __construct( protected Dependency1 $dep1, protected Dependency2 $dep2, protected array $config ) { } The annotation @Inject is telling the factory to inject the services between curly braces. Valid service names should be provided, as registered in the container. To inject an array value from the container, you can use dot notation as below. use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject; /** * @Inject({"config.debug"}) */ which will inject $container->get('config')['debug']; Even if using dot annotation, the annotated factory will check first if a service name exists with that name. You can use the @Inject annotation on setters too, they will be called at creation time and injected with the configured dependencies. Using the AnnotatedRepositoryFactory You can register doctrine repositories and inject them using the AnnotatedRepositoryFactory as below. return [ 'factories' => [ ExampleRepository::class => AnnotatedRepositoryFactory::class, ], ]; The next step is to add the @Entity annotation in the repository class. The name field has to be the fully qualified class name. Every repository should extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository , and must be the repository class of the entity. use Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository; use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Entity; /** * @Entity(name="App\Entity\Example") */ class ExampleRepository extends EntityRepository { } Cache annotations This package is built on top of doctrine/annotations . To cache annotations, you should register a service factory at key AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE that should return a valid PSR-6 cache pool, an implementation of Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface . Below, we give an example, using symfony/cache : return [ 'annotations_cache_dir' => __DIR__ . '/../../data/cache/annotations', 'dependencies' => [ 'factories' => [ // used by dot-annotated-services to cache annotations // needs to return a PSR-6 cache pool AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE => AnnotationsCacheFactory::class, ] ], ]; namespace Frontend\App\Factory; use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface; use Psr\Container\ContainerInterface; use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter; class AnnotationsCacheFactory { public function __invoke(ContainerInterface $container): CacheItemPoolInterface { //change this to suite your caching needs return new FilesystemAdapter( namespace: 'annotations', directory: $container->get('config')['annotations_cache_dir'], ); } }

docs.text: Caching the annotations dot-annotated-services reads class annotations using doctrine/annotations and caches them using doctrine/cache . Configuration To cache annotations, you should register a service factory at key AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE that should return a valid Doctrine\Common\Cache\Cache cache driver. See Cache Drivers for available implementations offered by doctrine. See below an example on how you can configure dot-annotated-services to cache annotations. You can add this configuration value to your application's Doctrine config file: 'annotations_cache_dir' => __DIR__ . '/../../data/cache/annotations', 'dependencies' => [ 'factories' => [ Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE => YourApp\Factory\AnnotationsCacheFactory::class, ], ]; where AnnotationsCacheFactory is a custom factory that needs to return a Doctrine Cache Driver : <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Factory; class AnnotationsCacheFactory { public function __invoke(Psr\Container\ContainerInterface $container) { return new Doctrine\Common\Cache\FilesystemCache($container->get('config')['annotations_cache_dir']); } }

docs.text: Factories dot-annotated-services is based on three reusable factories - AnnotatedRepositoryFactory , AnnotatedServiceFactory and AnnotatedServiceAbstractFactory - able to inject any dependency into a class. AttributedRepositoryFactory Injects entity repositories into a class. Exceptions thrown Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not exist Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not have @Entity annotation Psr\Container\NotFoundExceptionInterface if Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface does not exist in the service container Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface if service manager is unable to provide an instance of Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface AttributedServiceFactory Injects class dependencies into classes. If a dependency is specified using the dot notation, AttributedServiceFactory will try to load a service having that specific alias. If it does not find one, it will try to load the dependency as a config tree, checking each segment if it's available in the service container. You can use the @Inject annotation on setters too, they will be called at creation time and injected with the configured dependencies. Exceptions thrown Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if service does not exist Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if service does not have @Inject annotation on it's constructor ReflectionException on failure of creating a ReflectionClass of the dependency Psr\Container\NotFoundExceptionInterface if a dependency does not exist in the service container Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface if service manager is unable to provide an instance of a dependency AnnotatedServiceAbstractFactory Using this approach, no service manager configuration is required. It uses the registered abstract factory to create annotated services. To tell the abstract factory which services are to be created, you need to annotate the service class with the @Service annotation. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Service; /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Service */ class Example { /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({ * YourApp\Repository\Dependency1::class, * YourApp\Repository\Dependency2::class, * "config.example" * }) */ public function __construct( protected YourApp\Repository\Dependency1 $dependency1, protected YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $dependency2, protected array $exampleConfig, ) { } } And that's it, you don't need to configure the service manager with this class, creation will happen automatically.
docs.title: Factories

docs.text: Inject entity repositories Prepare repository dot-annotated-services determines the entity a repository is related to by looking at the @Entity annotation, added to the repository class. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Repository; /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Entity(name="YourApp\Entity\Example") */ class ExampleRepository extends Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository { } Each entity repository must extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository . Register repository Open the ConfigProvider of the module where your repository resides. Add a new entry under factories , where the key is your repository FQCN and the value is Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedRepositoryFactory::class . See the below example for a better understanding of the file structure. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp; class ConfigProvider { public function __invoke(): array { return [ 'dependencies' => $this->getDependencies(), ]; } public function getDependencies(): array { return [ 'factories' => [ YourApp\Repository\ExampleRepository::class => Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedRepositoryFactory::class, ], ]; } }

docs.text: Inject class dependencies Prepare class dot-annotated-services determines the dependencies by looking at the @Inject annotation, added to the constructor of a class. Dependencies are specified as one parameter, which is an array of FQCNs. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Service; class Example { /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({ * YourApp\Repository\Dependency1::class, * YourApp\Repository\Dependency2::class, * "config" * }) */ public function __construct( protected YourApp\Repository\Dependency1 $dependency1, protected YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $dependency2, protected array $config ) { } } If your class needs the value of a specific configuration key, you can specify the path using dot notation: /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({ * YourApp\Repository\Dependency1::class, * YourApp\Repository\Dependency2::class, * "config.example" * }) */ public function __construct( protected YourApp\Repository\Dependency1 $dependency1, protected YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $dependency2, protected array $exampleConfig, ) { } Register class Open the ConfigProvider of the module where your class resides. Add a new entry under factories , where the key is your class FQCN and the value is Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory::class . See the below example for a better understanding of the file structure. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp; class ConfigProvider { public function __invoke(): array { return [ 'dependencies' => $this->getDependencies(), ]; } public function getDependencies(): array { return [ 'factories' => [ YourApp\Service\Example::class => Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory::class, ], ]; } }

docs.text: Version 5 is discontinued Version 5.x of dot-annotated-services is discontinued and receives no further releases. The last release was 5.2.0 . Version 5.x was a separate line of this package that replaced annotations with PHP attributes. That functionality now lives in its own package, dot-dependency-injection , which is the supported alternative for attribute-based dependency injection. Which package to use You want Use PHP attributes dot-dependency-injection Annotations ( doctrine/annotations ) dot-annotated-services 6.0 , or 4.x if you have to stay on Doctrine ORM 2.x Versions 4.x and 6.0 are the proper releases of dot-annotated-services . They are annotation-based and are documented in version 6 and version 4 . Migrating from 5.x to dot-dependency-injection The attributes and factories keep their names and syntax. Only the package and the namespaces change. Replace the package: composer remove dotkernel/dot-annotated-services composer require dotkernel/dot-dependency-injection Replace the namespaces in your code and configuration: 5.x ( dot-annotated-services ) dot-dependency-injection Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Inject Dot\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Inject Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Entity Dot\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Entity Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AttributedServiceFactory Dot\DependencyInjection\Factory\AttributedServiceFactory Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AttributedRepositoryFactory Dot\DependencyInjection\Factory\AttributedRepositoryFactory Dot\AnnotatedServices\ConfigProvider Dot\DependencyInjection\ConfigProvider Check the requirements, including the supported PHP versions, in the dot-dependency-injection documentation . Migrating from 5.x to annotations If you prefer annotations, follow the upgrade guide for 6.0 .

docs.text: Caching the annotations dot-annotated-services reads class annotations using doctrine/annotations and can cache them in any PSR-6 cache pool. Configuration To cache annotations, register a service factory at key Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE (which is Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface::class ). It must return an implementation of Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface . Without this service, annotations are parsed on every request. If the config service has the key debug set to true , the cache checks whether the annotated files changed and refreshes stale entries. Keep it false in production. See below an example on how you can configure dot-annotated-services to cache annotations. You can add this configuration value to your application's config file: 'annotations_cache_dir' => __DIR__ . '/../../data/cache/annotations', 'dependencies' => [ 'factories' => [ Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE => YourApp\Factory\AnnotationsCacheFactory::class, ], ], where AnnotationsCacheFactory is a custom factory that needs to return a PSR-6 cache pool. The example below uses symfony/cache , but any PSR-6 implementation works: <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Factory; use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface; use Psr\Container\ContainerInterface; use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter; class AnnotationsCacheFactory { public function __invoke(ContainerInterface $container): CacheItemPoolInterface { return new FilesystemAdapter( namespace: 'annotations', directory: $container->get('config')['annotations_cache_dir'], ); } } Cache drivers from doctrine/cache , such as FilesystemCache , are not PSR-6 pools and cannot be used directly.

docs.text: Configuration dot-annotated-services needs no global registration. The factories are registered per class, under factories in your own ConfigProvider . See Inject class dependencies and Inject entity repositories . Dot\AnnotatedServices\ConfigProvider is still provided, but it returns an empty configuration. You can keep it in your configuration aggregator (usually: config/config.php ) if it is already there, or leave it out. The factories only depend on psr/container , so they work with any PSR-11 container that accepts a factory callable per service key, such as Laminas Service Manager. See Factories for details and Cache to cache the parsed annotations.

docs.text: Factories dot-annotated-services is based on two reusable factories - AnnotatedRepositoryFactory and AnnotatedServiceFactory - able to inject any dependency into a class. AnnotatedRepositoryFactory Injects entity repositories into a class. The repository must extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository and carry the @Entity annotation. The repository class returned by the entity manager must be the registered class: set the repository class on the entity ( #[ORM\Entity(repositoryClass: ...)] ) so that EntityManager::getRepository() returns an instance of it. Exceptions thrown Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not exist Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if repository does not have @Entity annotation Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if the entity manager returns a repository that is not an instance of the requested class Psr\Container\NotFoundExceptionInterface if Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface does not exist in the service container Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface if the container is unable to provide an instance of Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface AnnotatedServiceFactory Injects class dependencies into classes. A constructor with required parameters must carry the @Inject annotation. A constructor without required parameters can omit it. If a dependency is specified using the dot notation, AnnotatedServiceFactory will try to load a service having that specific alias. If it does not find one, it will try to load the dependency as a config tree, checking each segment if it's available in the service container. If a dependency is not registered in the service container but is the name of an existing class, AnnotatedServiceFactory creates it with new , without constructor arguments. You can use the @Inject annotation on public setters too. They are called, in declaration order, after the object is constructed and injected with the configured dependencies. The constructor is only called once, and static methods are ignored. Exceptions thrown Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if service does not exist Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if service does not have @Inject annotation on its constructor, and the constructor has required parameters Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException if a dependency is neither a service nor a class Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\InvalidArgumentException if a key of a dotted dependency does not exist, including when the path is longer than the data ReflectionException on failure of creating a ReflectionClass of the dependency Psr\Container\NotFoundExceptionInterface if a dependency does not exist in the service container Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface if the container is unable to provide an instance of a dependency
docs.title: Factories

docs.text: Overview dot-annotated-services is Dotkernel's dependency injection service using annotations. By providing reusable factories for service and repository injection, it reduces code complexity in projects. Version 6.0 continues the annotation-based API of version 4.x . Version 5.x is a separate package line that uses PHP attributes instead of annotations. See the upgrade guide if you are coming from 4.x or 5.x . Requirements PHP 8.3 , 8.4 , 8.5 or 8.6 PSR-11 version 1 or 2 doctrine/annotations ^2.0 doctrine/orm ^3.0 Version History Branch PSR-11 Docblock Comments OSS Lifecycle PHP Version 6.0 1 || 2 Annotations 5.0 1 || 2 Attributes 4.0 1 Annotations 3.0 1 Annotations Versions 4.x and 6.0 are the proper releases of this package. They are annotation-based. Version 5.x is discontinued. It used PHP attributes, which are now provided by a separate package: dot-dependency-injection ( documentation ). Use it if you want attributes instead of annotations. See Version 5 is discontinued for migration notes. Badges

docs.text: Upgrading to 6.0 Version 6.0 continues the annotation-based API of 4.x . The 5.x releases are a separate, attribute-based package line. Follow the section that matches the version you are coming from. From 4.x Requirements PHP 8.3 or newer is required. PHP 8.2 is no longer supported. doctrine/orm ^3.0 and doctrine/annotations ^2.0 are required. Applications still on Doctrine ORM 2.x or doctrine/annotations 1.x must upgrade those first, or stay on 4.x . doctrine/cache is no longer a requirement of this package, and doctrine/orm 3.x does not install it. If your application uses its classes, require it yourself. laminas/laminas-servicemanager is no longer a requirement. The factories only depend on psr/container , version 1.1 or 2 . If your application uses Laminas Service Manager, require it yourself. psr/cache and psr/container are now declared as direct requirements. Changes that can break your code Change Symptom Fix AnnotatedServiceAbstractFactory and the @Service annotation are removed Class not found, or the service is no longer created automatically Register the class under factories with AnnotatedServiceFactory , and remove @Service and the abstract factory registration. See below Dot\AnnotatedServices\ConfigProvider no longer registers the abstract factory abstract_factories is no longer filled by this package None, unless you read that configuration key The constructor is no longer called a second time when it carries @Inject Code that relied on the constructor running twice no longer does Remove that reliance. Classes with readonly promoted properties now work AnnotatedRepositoryFactory throws if the entity manager returns a repository that is not an instance of the registered class Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException: Entity manager returned a repository of type ... Set repositoryClass on the entity to the registered repository, or register the class the entity manager returns A dotted dependency whose path is longer than the data now throws InvalidArgumentException where config.a.b used to inject the value of config.a Fix the key path AnnotatedServiceFactory::__invoke() and createObject() return object instead of mixed Fatal error in subclasses that override them with an incompatible return type Return an object from the override AbstractAnnotatedFactory::CACHE_SERVICE is a typed constant ( string ) Fatal error in subclasses that redeclare it untyped Declare it as public const string Behavior that now works @Inject("config") without curly braces is accepted. A dotted key whose value is null is injected as null . It used to throw. Replacing @Service Before, on 4.x : /** * @Service */ class ExampleService { } After, on 6.0 : remove the annotation and register the class with the factory in your ConfigProvider : 'dependencies' => [ 'factories' => [ ExampleService::class => Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory::class, ], ], Also remove Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceAbstractFactory from abstract_factories if you registered it yourself. Documentation changes The cache documentation of 4.x described doctrine/cache drivers. The package has always required a PSR-6 cache pool. See Cache . From 5.x 5.x uses PHP attributes. 6.0 uses annotations, and adds setter injection and an annotation cache. Migrating from 5.x to 6.0 means moving back from attributes to annotations. Classes 5.x 6.0 Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Inject Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Entity Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Entity Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AttributedServiceFactory Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AttributedRepositoryFactory Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedRepositoryFactory Syntax Before, on 5.x : use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Entity; use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Attribute\Inject; #[Entity(name: Example::class)] class ExampleRepository extends EntityRepository { } class ExampleService { #[Inject(ExampleRepository::class, 'config')] public function __construct( protected ExampleRepository $repository, protected array $config, ) { } } After, on 6.0 : use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Entity; use Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject; /** * @Entity(name="App\Entity\Example") */ class ExampleRepository extends EntityRepository { } class ExampleService { /** * @Inject({ * ExampleRepository::class, * "config" * }) */ public function __construct( protected ExampleRepository $repository, protected array $config, ) { } } Registration Replace the factory class names in your ConfigProvider . Nothing needs to be added to your configuration aggregator. Differences to be aware of 6.0 requires Doctrine ORM 3.x . 5.x also supported 2.x . 6.0 has no check for services that inject themselves. A service listed in its own @Inject is not reported as a recursion. 6.0 additionally supports @Inject on setters, and caching the parsed annotations (see Cache ). 6.0 requires doctrine/annotations and a PSR-6 pool if you want to cache annotations.

docs.text: Usage Version 6.x of dot-annotated-services uses doctrine/annotations to parse and inject dependencies. It continues the annotation-based API of version 4.x . Version 5.x is a separate package line that uses PHP attributes instead. Annotations must be written in a docblock, which starts with /** . A comment starting with /* is ignored. You can use it to: Inject class dependencies Inject entity repositories Coming from 4.x or 5.x ? Read the upgrade guide .

docs.text: Inject entity repositories Prepare repository dot-annotated-services determines the entity a repository is related to by looking at the @Entity annotation, added to the repository class. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Repository; /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Entity(name="YourApp\Entity\Example") */ class ExampleRepository extends Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository { } Each entity repository must extend Doctrine\ORM\EntityRepository . The entity must declare this class as its repository, so that EntityManager::getRepository() returns an instance of it: #[Doctrine\ORM\Mapping\Entity(repositoryClass: YourApp\Repository\ExampleRepository::class)] class Example { } If the entity manager returns a repository that is not an instance of the registered class, AnnotatedRepositoryFactory throws a Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\RuntimeException . Register repository Open the ConfigProvider of the module where your repository resides. Add a new entry under factories , where the key is your repository FQCN and the value is Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedRepositoryFactory::class . See the below example for a better understanding of the file structure. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp; class ConfigProvider { public function __invoke(): array { return [ 'dependencies' => $this->getDependencies(), ]; } public function getDependencies(): array { return [ 'factories' => [ YourApp\Repository\ExampleRepository::class => Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedRepositoryFactory::class, ], ]; } }

docs.text: Inject class dependencies Prepare class dot-annotated-services determines the dependencies by looking at the @Inject annotation, added to the constructor of a class. Dependencies are specified as a list of service names or FQCNs. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp\Service; class Example { /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({ * YourApp\Repository\Dependency1::class, * YourApp\Repository\Dependency2::class, * "config" * }) */ public function __construct( protected YourApp\Repository\Dependency1 $dependency1, protected YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $dependency2, protected array $config ) { } } A single dependency can be written without the curly braces: /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject("config") */ public function __construct(protected array $config) { } If your class needs the value of a specific configuration key, you can specify the path using dot notation: /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({ * YourApp\Repository\Dependency1::class, * YourApp\Repository\Dependency2::class, * "config.example" * }) */ public function __construct( protected YourApp\Repository\Dependency1 $dependency1, protected YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $dependency2, protected array $exampleConfig, ) { } Rules for dot notation: The container is first asked for a service with the full name ( config.example ). Only if there is none is the name split at the dots. The first segment is the service (usually config ), the following segments are array keys. A key whose value is null is injected as null . A key that does not exist, or a path longer than the data (for example config.a.b when config['a'] is a string), throws Dot\AnnotatedServices\Exception\InvalidArgumentException . Setter injection @Inject can also be added to public setters. They are called after the constructor, and receive the configured dependencies as arguments: /** * @Dot\AnnotatedServices\Annotation\Inject({YourApp\Helper\Dependency2::class}) */ public function setHelper(YourApp\Helper\Dependency2 $helper): void { $this->helper = $helper; } The constructor is never called a second time, so classes with readonly promoted properties work. Static methods are ignored. Register class Open the ConfigProvider of the module where your class resides. Add a new entry under factories , where the key is your class FQCN and the value is Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory::class . See the below example for a better understanding of the file structure. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace YourApp; class ConfigProvider { public function __invoke(): array { return [ 'dependencies' => $this->getDependencies(), ]; } public function getDependencies(): array { return [ 'factories' => [ YourApp\Service\Example::class => Dot\AnnotatedServices\Factory\AnnotatedServiceFactory::class, ], ]; } } You can use only the fully qualified class name as the service key.
docs.title: Inject class dependencies
